events.title: Germany Invades Poland
events.description: German forces launched a massive invasion of Poland at dawn, using combined air, armor, and infantry attacks. Britain and France declared war on Germany two days later.
events.significance: Marked the start of World War II in Europe, the deadliest conflict in human history, which reshaped global politics and led to the creation of the United Nations.

events.title: Great Kanto Earthquake
events.description: A magnitude 7.9 earthquake struck the Kanto region of Japan, devastating Tokyo and Yokohama. Fires, a tsunami, and landslides compounded the destruction, killing an estimated 105,000 people.
events.significance: One of the deadliest natural disasters in Japanese history; it prompted major reforms in urban planning and earthquake-resistant construction, and is commemorated annually as Disaster Prevention Day.

events.title: Wreck of the Titanic Discovered
events.description: A joint American-French expedition led by Robert Ballard and Jean-Louis Michel located the wreck of the RMS Titanic about 12,500 feet below the surface of the North Atlantic, roughly 370 miles off Newfoundland.
events.significance: Solved a 73-year mystery about the ship's final resting place, revealed that it had broken in two, and advanced deep-sea robotic exploration technology.

events.title: Korean Air Lines Flight 007 Shot Down
events.description: A Boeing 747 airliner that strayed into Soviet airspace was shot down by a Soviet Su-15 interceptor near Sakhalin Island, killing all 269 people aboard.
events.significance: Heightened Cold War tensions and led President Reagan to make the U.S. Global Positioning System available for civilian use to prevent similar navigational errors.

events.title: Death of Louis XIV of France
events.description: Louis XIV, the Sun King, died just days before his 77th birthday after reigning for 72 years and 110 days, the longest verified reign of any monarch in European history.
events.significance: His death ended an era of French absolutism and dominance in Europe, passing the throne to his five-year-old great-grandson Louis XV.
